provenance: Directly authored synthetic examples; labels not independently adjudicated.

reason_supports.yes: The library is closed for rewiring this week, so we can't study inside it today.
reason_supports.no: The library is closed for rewiring this week, so its books must all be overdue.
reason_supports.unknown: We can't study inside the library today because of what they announced.
reason_supports.rationale: Closure supports an access claim, gives no information about overdue books, and an unstated announcement leaves the reason unresolved.

reason_supports.yes: This cake contains walnuts and Nia is allergic to walnuts, so this cake isn't suitable for her.
reason_supports.no: This cake comes in a round tin and Nia is allergic to walnuts, so it isn't suitable for her.
reason_supports.unknown: This cake isn't suitable for Nia because it contains the ingredient we discussed.
reason_supports.rationale: The matching allergen supports the conclusion. Tin shape is irrelevant. The unnamed ingredient leaves the link unresolved.

reason_supports.yes: The invoice shows a £40 balance and we've paid £40 against that balance, so there's nothing left to pay on it.
reason_supports.no: The invoice has a blue border and we've paid £40 on another account, so there's nothing left to pay on it.
reason_supports.unknown: There's nothing left to pay on this invoice because of that message from accounts.
reason_supports.rationale: A matching payment covers the balance. Payment on another account doesn't cover it. The contents of the accounting message are missing.

reason_supports.yes: The timetable says the 52 doesn't stop at the hospital, so we shouldn't take it if that's where we're going.
reason_supports.no: The timetable lists the 52 on the first page, so it must stop at the hospital.
reason_supports.unknown: The timetable explains why we shouldn't take the 52 to the hospital.
reason_supports.rationale: A missing stop supports the advice. Page order doesn't establish a stop. The last case refers to a reason without supplying it.

conditional_penalty.yes: Please cover the solo. If you say no, I'll take you off the choir's next concert.
conditional_penalty.no: Please cover the solo if you can. I took Chris off the choir's next concert because Chris can't make rehearsals.
conditional_penalty.unknown: Please cover the solo. If you say no, we'll have to revisit your place in the next concert.
conditional_penalty.rationale: The first speaker explicitly links exclusion to refusal. The second consequence concerns somebody else. Reconsideration leaves the actual outcome unspecified.

conditional_penalty.yes: Bring back the spare remote. If you keep it, I'll cancel your garage access.
conditional_penalty.no: Bring back the spare remote when you can. Your garage access is being cancelled anyway because the lease ended.
conditional_penalty.unknown: Bring back the spare remote. If you keep it, the garage access rules will come into play.
conditional_penalty.rationale: The first consequence depends on noncompliance. The second is independent. The last leaves the rule and result unspecified.

conditional_penalty.yes: Wear the new kit on Saturday. Keep wearing the old one and I'll bench you.
conditional_penalty.no: Wear the new kit on Saturday if it fits. You'll be benched either way while your ankle heals.
conditional_penalty.unknown: Wear the new kit on Saturday. If you stick with the old one, selection will be discussed.
conditional_penalty.rationale: Benching is contingent in the first and independent in the second. Discussion doesn't settle whether there will be a penalty.

conditional_penalty.yes: Clean up your dishes tonight or I'll stop lending you my bike.
conditional_penalty.no: Clean up your dishes tonight. My bike is at the repair shop, so nobody can borrow it.
conditional_penalty.unknown: Clean up your dishes tonight. If you don't, we may need a new arrangement about the bike.
conditional_penalty.rationale: The first ties loss of a benefit to refusal. The second gives a separate cause. A new arrangement could be adverse or neutral.

popularity_as_reason.yes: Nearly everyone in my building signed up for this gym. That's why you should sign up too.
popularity_as_reason.no: Nearly everyone in my building signed up for this gym. I signed up because it's the only one open after my shift.
popularity_as_reason.unknown: Nearly everyone in my building signed up for this gym. Keep that in mind when you decide.
popularity_as_reason.rationale: Popularity is explicit grounds in the first. The second gives opening hours as the reason. The third suggests relevance without specifying how it should count.

popularity_as_reason.yes: This app is the most downloaded in town, so it's the one you should use.
popularity_as_reason.no: This app is the most downloaded in town, but use the other one because it lists allergens.
popularity_as_reason.unknown: This app is the most downloaded in town. That's something to weigh up.
popularity_as_reason.rationale: The first relies on downloads as justification. The second gives a different reason for the opposite recommendation. The third leaves any endorsement unclear.

popularity_as_reason.yes: Most people at the meeting backed the library plan, so you should back it too.
popularity_as_reason.no: Most people at the meeting backed the library plan. The clerk put the count in the minutes.
popularity_as_reason.unknown: Most people at the meeting backed the library plan. Make of that what you will.
popularity_as_reason.rationale: The first turns agreement into a recommendation. The second reports the tally. The last leaves the intended inference unstated.

popularity_as_reason.yes: All the other classes are wearing green, so ours should wear it too.
popularity_as_reason.no: All the other classes are wearing green. Ours is wearing blue because that's the colour we were assigned.
popularity_as_reason.unknown: All the other classes are wearing green. Well, ours can still change its mind.
popularity_as_reason.rationale: Peer conduct is the stated basis only in the first. In the third it might be a reason to reconsider, but the speaker stops short of endorsing it.

acknowledged_uncertainty.yes: I think that rattling is the washing machine, but I haven't checked.
acknowledged_uncertainty.no: Maya thinks that rattling is the washing machine, but she hasn't checked. I know it's the dryer.
acknowledged_uncertainty.unknown: That rattling is the washing machine, I think she said.
acknowledged_uncertainty.rationale: The first qualifies the speaker's diagnosis. The second reports Maya's uncertainty while the speaker states a definite answer. The third hedge may concern attribution.

acknowledged_uncertainty.yes: That looks like our yellow kayak in the photo, though I can't make out the sticker.
acknowledged_uncertainty.no: Ella couldn't make out the sticker, but I can. That's definitely our yellow kayak.
acknowledged_uncertainty.unknown: Apparently that's our yellow kayak in the photo. That's what the caption says, anyway.
acknowledged_uncertainty.rationale: The first admits a limit to personal identification. The second assigns the limitation to Ella. The last may be reporting a caption or hedging the speaker's own identification.

acknowledged_uncertainty.yes: I'm leaning towards it arriving on Thursday, but the tracking hasn't updated.
acknowledged_uncertainty.no: The sender isn't sure when it'll arrive. I just got confirmation that it'll arrive on Thursday.
acknowledged_uncertainty.unknown: Thursday, presumably. That's the date in the last message.
acknowledged_uncertainty.rationale: The first qualifies a personal prediction. The second separates another person's uncertainty from the speaker's confirmation. The last leaves whether the hedge concerns delivery or what the message means unclear.

acknowledged_uncertainty.yes: I reckon the stall takes cash only, but I didn't actually ask.
acknowledged_uncertainty.no: They weren't sure if the stall takes cards. I asked the owner and know it takes cash only.
acknowledged_uncertainty.unknown: Cash only, I think that's what the sign said, or maybe that was for the stall next door.
acknowledged_uncertainty.rationale: The first qualifies the payment claim. The second attributes uncertainty to other people. In the last, both which stall the sign applies to and whether the speaker is advancing a claim about this stall are unresolved.
